name: a scattered dot cloud settles into a sorted column chart
looks: A loose scatter of coloured dots, standing for individual accounts, drifts under a headline count. The scatter then relaxes into neat columns, one column per account, sorted tallest to shortest, so a handful of outsized columns (shown in a second colour) visibly dominate the rest.
build: Dots start at a soft circular scatter position and tween to grid column positions sorted by count, power3.out, per-dot easing offsets so the field settles unevenly; the outsized columns swap to the accent/ink colour as they land. A mono caption states what one column equals.
sound: A soft granular patter while the scatter drifts, a firmer tick as the columns snap into their sorted order.
prompt: Let a loose scatter of dots, one per unit, relax into a sorted column chart, tallest first, so a few outsized columns visibly dominate everything else. Name what one column equals in a small caption, and recolour only the dominant columns so the imbalance reads instantly.
